{"lineage":"original","name":"A prohibition written into a design node's prose is noticed as having no home a check can read","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"When a Requirement, Capability, Component, Interface or accepted Decision carries a prohibition in its own text — "must never", "is not allowed to" — and no Constraint binds that node, the loop says so, once, as a finding about the practice. The routing table already sends such a sentence to a Constraint rather than a Requirement, because a Constraint can `constrains` what it binds and be read by the checks; an instruction with nothing noticing its absence is one leg of three.

Measured before it was asked for: reflow2's own design held ≈61 such sentences in prose (9 of 10 sampled genuine) against 8 Constraint nodes, on a routing row that had been added precisely because eleven prohibitions were left as Requirements (fact:capture-is-blind-to-three-families-and-the-routing-table-has-a-row-for-two-of-them).

Anthony's word, 2026-09-14: "Build the detector for prohibitions living in prose."

What it must NOT do: nudge a brainstormed idea (a proposed Decision's "must never" is a musing), flag a DesignRule or a Constraint (both are homes), read records and checks as intent, match "shall not" (the requirement idiom), or judge whether the sentence should become a Constraint — filing or acknowledging stays the reader's call.","status":"accepted"}
